record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.original_question: Let Ω be the unit disc in R^2 and, for ε>0, consider the Ginzburg–Landau Dirichlet problem -Δu=(1/ε^2)u(1-|u|^2) in Ω with boundary condition u(x)=x on ∂Ω. Let U_ε(x)=(x/|x|)f_ε(|x|) denote the radial solution obtained from the unique ODE solution f_ε with f_ε(0)=0 and f_ε(1)=1. Is U_ε the only solution of this boundary-value problem?

evidence.quote: We will denote by Uε(x) the solution of (2.1) given by (2.2)–(2.3), and we call it the radially symmetric (or just the radial) solution of (2.1). A long-standing open problem is whether Uε(x) is also the unique solution of (2.1). Open Problem 2.1 ... Is the radial solution Uε the only solution of (2.1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝ² denote the open unit disc, and for a parameter ε > 0 consider the Ginzburg–Landau Dirichlet boundary-value problem for maps u : Ω → ℝ²,

  −Δu = (1/ε²) u (1 − |u|²)  in Ω,
  u(x) = x  on ∂Ω.

The associated radial profile equation is the ODE
  −f''(r) − (1/r) f'(r) + f(r)/r² = (1/ε²) f(r)(1 − f(r)²),  r ∈ (0,1),
with boundary conditions f(0) = 0 and f(1) = 1, which is known to admit a unique solution f_ε. Define the radial vortex
  U_ε(x) = f_ε(|x|) · x/|x|,  x ∈ Ω \ {0}, U_ε(0) = 0.

Question: Is U_ε the only solution of the above boundary-value problem? Equivalently, prove or disprove that every solution u ∈ C²(Ω; ℝ²) of −Δu = ε⁻² u(1 − |u|²) in Ω with u(x) = x on ∂Ω must coincide with U_ε.
artifact.status_search_result: The two-dimensional uniqueness question for the radial Ginzburg–Landau vortex on the unit disc, originating from work of Bethuel–Brezis–Hélein and Brezis, is widely regarded as a long-standing open problem. Recent progress establishes uniqueness of the degree-one vortex in the unit ball B^N for dimensions N ≥ 7 (Ignat–Nguyen–Slastikov–Zarnescu and subsequent works), and partial minimality/symmetry results in dimensions N = 2,…,6 for restricted classes (e.g. gradient fields, vortex sheets), but the full uniqueness in the original 2D disc case is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of degree-one Ginzburg–Landau vortex in the unit ball in dimensions N ≥ 7
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes uniqueness of the symmetric vortex solution in the unit ball B^N for dimensions N ≥ 7, leaving lower dimensions open.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness is known in dimensions N ≥ 7 but the original 2D case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Minimality of the vortex solution for Ginzburg–Landau systems (R. Ignat, MFO report 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys progress on uniqueness/minimality of the radial vortex, noting unresolved cases in low dimensions including N=2.
status_evidence.claim: The two-dimensional uniqueness problem for the radial GL vortex is still considered open.

status_evidence.title: Vortex sheet solutions for the Ginzburg–Landau system in cylinders
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses dichotomy between escaping and non-escaping solutions in dimensions 2 ≤ N ≤ 6.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist in low dimensions but uniqueness in 2D disc is not established.
